Some effective ways are: prompt-engineered planning and explicit word counting, dynamic feedback during generation, and training-based optimization for length-constrained tasks. A prompt-only method asks the model to deliberately plan its response structure and count words as it writes, improving adherence without retraining, especially for shorter-to-medium targets [1]. Another training-free approach adds dynamic length feedback during generation so the model can adaptively adjust toward a target token, word, or sentence count [2].

If retraining is possible, papers also describe stronger task-specific methods. Reinforcement learning can optimize compliance with strict duration or syllable constraints in translation while preserving meaning [3]. More generally, supervised fine-tuning on top of dynamic feedback can help length control generalize to broader text-generation tasks [2]. A lightweight mitigation for overly long outputs is also to add a fixed conciseness reminder to the prompt, which reduces excessive output tails across many prompting strategies [7].
